explain.say: Imagine a comic. The words people say float in speech bubbles. In a story, we use speech marks instead, little bubbles made of commas in the air. Look at the first box on the board: open the speech marks before anyone talks.

explain.say: The second box: inside the marks go only the words the person really says, starting with a capital letter. Can we go to the market? See? Just the talking words. What would you say if you found a puppy?

explain.say: Now the third box, the tricky bit. The punctuation goes inside, before the marks close. A comma, a question mark or an exclamation mark. Can we go to the market? The question mark stays inside the bubble.

explain.say: Then close the marks, and look at the last box: who said it. Can we go to the market? asked Ana. Asked Ana is called the reporting clause. Can you think of a better word than said? Whispered? Shouted?

explain.say: Well done! One more rule: a new speaker means a new line. That way your reader always knows who is talking. Look at the whole chain again. Challenge: write two lines where your friend asks you to play and you answer.

faq.q: How do I use speech marks?
faq.a: Put speech marks around only the words someone actually says, start with a capital letter, put punctuation inside the closing marks, then say who spoke.

faq.q: Where does the comma go in speech?
faq.a: Inside the speech marks, before they close: "I love mangoes," said Ben. If the speech ends with a question or a shout, use ? or ! instead of the comma.
asks: Comma inside or outside speech marks?

faq.q: When do I start a new line for speech?
faq.a: Start a new line every time a different person speaks. It helps the reader follow who is talking.

faq.q: What are words to use instead of said?
faq.a: Try asked, whispered, shouted, laughed, replied or muttered. They show how the words were spoken. Said is still fine, and often best.

faq.q: What is the difference between direct and reported speech?
faq.a: Direct speech gives the exact words in speech marks: "I am hungry," said Lin. Reported speech retells it without marks: Lin said that she was hungry.

facts: Speech marks are also called inverted commas or quotation marks.
Some languages use different marks: French and Russian often use « these » for speech.

quiz.why: Speech marks go around all the spoken words, with the question mark inside.

wrong.0: The question mark belongs inside the speech marks.
wrong.1: All the spoken words go inside the marks, not just one.
